full_judgment:
2. Respondent Nos. 2 to 5 filed the aforesaid case before the Court of Settlement for excluding holding No. 55, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka from the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings. Their case, in short, is that their mother, late Zarina Khatoon, obtained lease of the said plot of land from the Government on 20-5-1963 and thereafter she orally gifted the same to them with the permission of the Government and their names were duly mutated in the Government records and they possessed the said property and there was no reason to include the said property in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings in the Gazette notification published on 23rd September, 1986 and such inclusion is without jurisdiction. The case was contested by the Government petitioner stating that Zarina Khatoon constructed the building in the said plot and thereafter transferred the building to her children by an oral gift on 1-4-1969 with the permission of the Government and delivered possession to the donees who were in continuous possession of the same building by mutating their names in the Government record. Government's only defence was that the case being filed beyond the period of limitation the same was not maintainable. 

 3. Court of Settlement on consideration of the materials on record held that the property is not an abandoned property and since there is no basis for including the said property in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings in the gazette notification published on 23rd September, 1986 no question of limitation arises and so allowed the case and directed the Government to exclude the said property from the said list. Being aggrieved by the same Government moved the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 192 of 1991. By the impugned judgment High Court Division discharged the Rule. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner has filed this petition for leave to appeal. 

 4. Learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the Government petitioner submits that in the facts and circumstances of the case High Court Division acted illegally in not holding that the case before the Court of Settlement having been filed long after the period of limitation was not maintainable. 

 5. It appears that on Government's own admission the property in question was not an abandoned property and was wrongly included in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings. In that view of the matter question of limitation does not arise. By the impugned judgment justice having been done we are not inclined to interfere with the same on technical ground of limitation.
